gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the one driver-free two-screen 18.5-inch unit (UPERFECT Delta Max) shows the same picture on both panels over a single USB-C cable and needs two video feeds plus power (three cables) for two separate desktops, while every Aura 18.5-inch two- or three-screen model needs a display driver and its own 30 W, 45 W or 100 W wall adapter.
standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com (attachable), itechguides.com, twelvetabs.com and deal.ai. None of the first three names an 18-inch or 18.5-inch product; their largest screens are 16 to 16.1 inches. itechguides says 'DisplayLink is not equivalent to native DisplayPort Alt Mode' and that Mac support depends on the 'number of supported external displays', but gives no number and ties neither point to a model. deal.ai has part of it for one model: MagHub Quad Max 'Needs display driver install and 45W USB-C PD power'. No page states the one-cable mirroring of the driver-free dual, the driver and adapter wattage per Aura 18.5 model, or Apple's one-external-display figure. Not read: digitalcameraworld, tomshardware, techradar's roundup, gearlark, lbdsoftware, tutt.ca, walmart and the other theofficejournal pages.
decides: It splits the pick by video path instead of by screen count. Driver-free at 18.5 inches means one added screen (Aura Single Aero Pro Studio 18.5, sold out on Aura's US store today), or the UPERFECT Delta Max dual fed by two video outputs from the laptop. On a base M1 MacBook Air, which Apple says drives one external display, the Delta Max's second panel cannot natively show a different desktop. Every 18.5-inch triple read today (Aura Triple Boost, Triple Aero and Triple Go Studio; INVZI MagHub Quad Max per deal.ai) is a driver product that also needs wall power, so ChatGPT's 'driver-free' note applies only to its UPERFECT dual and single picks. For our rows: the FOPO S788 is the one linked product whose maker's fit range reaches 18.5-inch laptops, and per our record (not re-read today) it is also a driver (UsbDisplay) product with an external PD supply, so it sits in the same class as the Aura triples with 16-inch panels. The FOPO S999, the only 18.5-inch-panel product in a partner store, could not be read today, so its video path is still open. ChatGPT's prices are also stale: Aura's US store shows $579.00 for the Triple Boost Pro Studio 18.5 (ChatGPT: $629.00) and $629.00 for the Triple Aero Pro Studio 18.5 (ChatGPT: $699.00); UPERFECT's own store lists the touch Delta Max at $499.99 and unavailable, against ChatGPT's $399.99 Newegg card, which may be a different variant.
